title: 6.8 A Real-Time Pixel-Compensated Source-Driver IC with Dual-Slope Error Detection and Multi-Channel Time-Multiplexing Compensator for Compact OLED Displays
problem: LTPS-TFT OLED displays suffer from pixel-to-pixel variations in DTFT parameters (Kp, Vth) and channel-wise voltage offsets (Vos), causing non-uniform drain current and luminance even with identical input data. Internal compensation via additional TFTs/capacitors reduces aperture ratio and efficiency.
motivation: High-resolution mobile displays demand higher channel density and smaller pixel apertures, making TFT parameter variation a critical yield and quality issue.
method: A chip outside the display measures each pixel's transistor characteristics using a two-point detection method (testing the transistor at two signal levels to reveal its unique properties), then uses those measurements to dynamically adjust the voltage sent to each pixel, correcting its brightness. A single corrector circuit handles this for all pixels by processing them one at a time in rapid sequence (time-multiplexing), and because the correction occurs outside the pixel rather than inside it, the pixel preserves its full light-producing area.
key_novelty: Two-point error detection paired with time-shared voltage correction enables external per-pixel brightness compensation without modifying the pixel structure.
contributions: Dual-slope error detection method for DTFT parameter sensing
Multi-channel time-multiplexing compensator for real-time per-pixel Vdata adjustment
External compensation preserving pixel aperture ratio and efficiency
Compact source-driver IC with integrated compensation logic
primary_theme: Per-pixel OLED display compensation via source-driver
